course_name_original: Teoría de Estructuras y Construcciones Industriales (GME203)
course_name_en: Theory of Structures and Industrial Buildings
prerequisites: ELASTICIDAD Y RESISTENCIA DE MATERIALES I

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and understanding: Knowledge and understanding of the engineering disciplines specific to their specialty, at the level necessary to acquire the rest of the degree competencies, including notions of the latest advances.
Knowledge and understanding: Be aware of the multidisciplinary context of engineering.

Engineering analysis: The ability to analyze complex products, processes, and systems in their field of study; choose and apply relevant established analytical, computational, and experimental methods and correctly interpret the results of such analyses.

Engineering analysis: The ability to identify, formulate and solve engineering problems in their specialty; appropriately choose and apply established analytical, computational, and experimental methods; recognize the importance of social, health and safety, environmental, economic, and industrial constraints.

Engineering projects: Ability to plan, design and develop complex products (parts, components, finished products, etc.), processes and systems of their specialty, that meet established requirements, including being aware of social, health and safety, environmental, economic and industrial aspects; as well as selecting and applying appropriate design methods.
Engineering projects: Ability to design using advanced knowledge from their engineering specialty.

Research and innovation: Ability to perform bibliographic searches, consult and critically use databases and other sources of information, to carry out simulation and analysis with the aim of conducting research on technical topics in their specialty.
Research and innovation: Ability to consult and apply codes of good practice and safety in their specialty.
Research and innovation: Ability and skill to plan and conduct experimental research, interpret results, and draw conclusions in their field of study.
Practical application of engineering: Understanding of applicable techniques and methods of analysis, design and research and their limitations in the scope of their specialty.
Practical application of engineering: Practical competence to solve complex problems, carry out complex engineering projects and conduct research specific to their specialty.
Practical application of engineering: Knowledge of applying materials, equipment and tools, technology and engineering processes and their limitations in the scope of their specialty.
Practical application of engineering: Ability to apply engineering practice standards in their specialty.
Practical application of engineering: Knowledge of the social, health and safety, environmental, economic, and industrial implications of engineering practice.
Judgment formulation: Ability to manage complex technical or professional activities or projects in their specialty, taking responsibility for decision-making.
Communication and Teamwork: Ability to effectively communicate information, ideas, problems and solutions in the field of engineering and with society in general.

Communication and Teamwork: Ability to function effectively in national and international contexts, individually and in teams, and to cooperate with engineers as well as with people from other disciplines.
Continuous training: Ability to recognize the need for continuous self-training and to undertake this activity throughout their professional life independently.
Continuous training: Ability to stay up-to-date with developments in science and technology.
Defines the problem, the development of the solution, as well as the conclusions effectively, arguing and justifying each of them, and making correct use of language, in writing.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to the finite element method
teaching_methods: Development, writing and presentation of reports, documents, audiovisual material, etc. related to projects/POPBLs, carried out individually or in teams
Individual study and work, tests, exams and/or control points
Completion of exercises individually and in teams
Practical work in workshops and/or laboratories

assessment_methods.method: Technical capacity, involvement in the project/PBL, work performed, results obtained, documentation delivered, technical presentation and defense
Individual written and oral tests for the evaluation of technical competencies of the subject
Reports on exercises, case studies, computer practices, simulation practices, and laboratory practices

assessment_rules: Continuous evaluation and project feedback are provided. For the evaluation of competence RGM323, a minimum score of 3 in the control points is required to contribute to the average. If the average of activities for RGM323 is below 5, a recovery activity must be performed. Recovery for project-based assessments is through the same activity.
